Research question: "What analyses or measurements would best test whether AP-1 acts as a cellular memory mechanism?"

Propose 5 distinct, concrete ideas (analyses, measurements, or experiments) that a research lab could pursue to address this question. For each idea give a short title and a description of one or two sentences.

ideas.title: Transient stimulus with delayed recall of chromatin accessibility
ideas.description: Expose cells (e.g., fibroblasts or macrophages) to a brief AP-1-activating stimulus (TPA, EGF, or injury cue), wash out, and after days to weeks profile ATAC-seq and H3K27ac CUT&Tag. Then restimulate and test whether the sites that stayed open or were primed show faster or stronger transcription (nascent RNA-seq) than naive cells.

ideas.title: Acute degron-based AP-1 depletion at different time windows
ideas.description: Use dTAG/auxin degrons on FOS, JUN or the pioneer-like AP-1 factors to remove AP-1 either during the initial stimulus, after it, or only during recall. If memory needs ongoing AP-1, removal after the priming phase should erase it. If AP-1 is needed only to establish memory, removal at that point should have no effect.

ideas.title: Single-cell multiome tracking of lineage-linked memory
ideas.description: Perform paired scRNA/scATAC-seq, with lineage barcodes or live reporters, on cells at several times after a transient stimulus. Test whether AP-1 motif accessibility and target expression are inherited across cell divisions in clonal families, and whether they are bimodal, as expected for epigenetic memory.

ideas.title: Live-cell imaging of AP-1 dynamics and target reporters
ideas.description: Image endogenously tagged FOS/JUN and a transcriptional reporter of a target gene (MS2/PP7) through repeated pulses of stimulation. Quantify whether the history of pulses, such as their number or spacing, changes later binding dwell times or burst frequency, which would indicate a memory beyond simple signaling.

ideas.title: Targeted epigenome editing at AP-1-dependent enhancers
ideas.description: Use dCas9 tools to either block AP-1 motifs or force chromatin opening or closing (dCas9-p300, dCas9-KRAB) at selected primed enhancers, with and without prior stimulation. Measure whether the enhancer's state is sufficient to reproduce or abolish the memory response, which separates the contribution of AP-1 binding from that of downstream chromatin marks.
